content.title: About
content.content: Goat cheese is a soft or semi‑hard cheese made from whole or skimmed goat’s milk. It has a slightly tangy, mildly sharp flavor and a creamy texture. Goat cheese is commonly used in salads, pastas, casseroles, or enjoyed on its own as a snack.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Goat’s milk contains less lactose than cow’s milk, making goat cheese easier to digest for some lactose‑intolerant people.
Traditional goat cheese production originates from the Mediterranean, especially Greece (feta) and France (chèvre).
Goat cheese can be fresh or aged; aging transforms the flavor from mild to robust.
It is usually white or slightly yellow because goat milk lacks the carotenoids that color cow’s milk cheese.
In many cultures goat cheese is considered a “healthier” alternative due to higher levels of certain vitamins and minerals.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Goat cheese provides high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Calcium supports bone and dental health.

items.title: Contains vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 is important for nervous system function and red blood cell formation.

items.title: Lower lactose content
items.content: Reduced lactose makes it more suitable for people with mild lactose intolerance.

items.title: Contains polyunsaturated fats
items.content: Beneficial fatty acids in goat cheese may support cardiovascular health.

items.title: Milk allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to milk proteins or casein may react to goat cheese.

items.title: High sodium
items.content: Some goat cheeses are salty; people monitoring sodium intake should limit portions.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Like most cheeses, goat cheese is calorie‑dense and should be consumed in moderation.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy goat cheese fresh, crumble it over salads, spread it on bread, or incorporate it into casseroles, pizza, and pasta. It pairs well with honey, nuts, or fresh fruit.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store goat cheese in an airtight container in the refrigerator at 35‑40 °F (2‑4 °C). Fresh soft varieties are best used within a week, while aged cheeses can keep for up to a month. Discard if mold beyond the natural rind, an ammonia smell, or texture changes appear.
